instruction: Navigate to the NFL Teams page on the NFL website.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent started at nfl.com/international, navigated to the Super Bowl section (nfl.com/super-bowl), browsed Event Info, then tried Google search but hit SSL certificate error. Spent remaining turns stuck on error page. Never reached the historical scores page.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate nfl.com via top menu, click Super Bowl section, browse sub-pages (Event Info), interact with address bar, dismiss cookie banners
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to find the historical scores section (/scores/2019/post4). It navigated to the current Super Bowl page instead, then attempted Google search which failed due to SSL certificate error in the VM environment.
metadata.task_rationale: Model demonstrated ability to use nfl.com top navigation menu (WATCH, GAMES, NEWS, TEAMS, STATS). This task tests navigating to the Teams section, a simple menu click task within demonstrated capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires clicking the Teams link in nfl.com top navigation. Evaluator checks if active URL matches nfl.com/teams pattern.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the current Chrome tab URL from the accessibility tree, which is the right state to verify navigation.
Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) correctly performs regex matching against the extracted URL, appropriate for URL verification.
Expected regex pattern 'https://.*nfl\.com/teams' correctly matches the NFL teams page URL.
Metric parameter handling is correct: with expected.type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly, and the metric accesses rules['expected'] which yields the pattern list.
Single-requirement instruction (navigate to teams page) is fully covered by the URL check.

Minor concern: goto_prefix is 'https://www.' which may produce a double 'www.' if the address bar already shows 'www.nfl.com/teams', resulting in 'https://www.www.nfl.com/teams'. However, the regex '.*' is permissive enough to still match, so this does not cause a functional issue.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using goto_prefix='https://' instead of 'https://www.' to avoid potential double 'www.' in the constructed URL, even though the current regex handles it.
